tasks.label: ESPHome: Build and Upload over USB
tasks.detail: Finds the USB serial port itself. On an ESP32-S3 flashing over its native USB: the port can drop mid-handshake ('Device not configured') - just run the task again - and after a successful flash the log tail ends with 'ERROR Serial port closed!' because the chip re-enumerates. Both are harmless; use the OTA task or 'esphome logs --device <ip>' for logs on those boards.
tasks.command:
PORTS=$(find /dev -maxdepth 1 \( -name 'cu.usbmodem*' -o -name 'cu.usbserial*' -o -name 'cu.wchusbserial*' -o -name 'cu.SLAB_USBtoUART*' -o -name 'ttyUSB*' -o -name 'ttyACM*' \) | sort); COUNT=$(printf '%s
' "$PORTS" | grep -c .); if [ "$COUNT" -eq 0 ]; then echo 'No USB serial port found. Plug the board in (data cable, not charge-only), or run "ESPHome: Build and Upload over USB (pick port)".'; exit 1; fi; PORT=$(printf '%s
' "$PORTS" | head -1); if [ "$COUNT" -gt 1 ]; then echo 'Several USB serial ports found:'; printf '%s
' "$PORTS"; echo "Using $PORT - run the (pick port) task to choose another."; fi; echo "Flashing ${file} over $PORT"; .venv/bin/esphome run ${file} --device "$PORT"

tasks.label: ESPHome: Build and Upload over USB (pick port)
tasks.detail: Same, but asks for the port. Use it when more than one board is plugged in; 'ls /dev/cu.*' lists the candidates.

inputs.description: USB serial port (ls /dev/cu.* - an ESP32-S3's native USB is cu.usbmodem*, a CP2102 bridge is cu.usbserial-*)
